PullRequest.Title: sessions: rename worktree cleanup action
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Replaces the user-facing **Clean Up Agent Worktrees** term with **Open worktree cleanup** across the command, editor, storage suggestion, accessibility help, and tests. The new wording is less alarming and clarifies that the action opens a review surface rather than immediately deleting worktrees.

## Testing

- Passed `npm run transpile-client`
- Passed `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionStorageCleanupNotice.test.ts` (2 tests)

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench contribution registration and command discovery during startup / Command Palette use
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Module evaluation localizes the context-key description, editor descriptor, and action title, then registers the existing editor and action. The changed text performs no additional work before registration completes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed number of localized strings and registrations, independent of session or worktree count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous in-process registration; no queue, limiter, IPC, filesystem, subprocess, database, or network operation is introduced by the changed strings.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Localization and registration behavior and keys are unchanged; no cache key, miss behavior, or coalescing changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed hunks and unchanged action ID, precondition, menus, descriptor, and run implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material: the replacement strings differ only slightly in length and do not change registration cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff changes only default localized text and does not add startup work, allocation cardinality, or an expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening worktree cleanup from the command, Sessions menu, context menu, or cleanup notice
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing command suppresses the suggestion, opens the singleton editor, and setInput awaits loading measured worktree data before the editor is ready. The renamed title, editor name, and heading do not alter this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Measure session worktree disk usage through ISessionsManagementService.getSessionWorktreeDiskUsage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one measurement per session that owns a worktree on a cold/signature-invalidated scan; calls are limited to two concurrently. A warm scan reuses measurements for up to one hour.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical per-session measurement, one-hour cache, signature check, and concurrency-2 limiter existed before the label-only changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold measurements are awaited by SessionWorktreeCleanupEditor.load and therefore affect editor readiness; warm measurements are served from the existing cache.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cold work scales with the number of sessions owning worktrees after filtering; warm access maps cached entries. The diff does not change effective cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Disk-usage measurements use a shared Limiter(2); editor inputs are singleton-matched, and service refreshes are coalesced by _refreshPromise.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The one-hour measured-worktree cache, session signature invalidation, and refresh-promise coalescing are unchanged. Both cold and warm behavior are identical to the base revision.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from tracing the action run method through editor setInput/load to the cleanup service measurement implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-specific disk-usage duration is unknown, but the changed text cannot alter the established call count, scheduling, or critical-path placement.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Existing filesystem measurement remains on the same path with the same cardinality, cache, and limiter; the diff only renames visible strings.

Scenarios.Scenario: Displaying and announcing the session storage cleanup suggestion
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Constructing the notice creates fixed DOM controls, installs an autorun, and activates the cleanup service. Availability updates fixed DOM properties and emits one status announcement on a hidden-to-visible transition. The changed button and announcement wording do not alter activation or update frequency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Measure disk usage for sessions with worktrees when the cleanup suggestion service performs an enabled, uncached scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One disk-usage request per worktree-owning session on a cold scan, limited to two concurrent requests; refreshes are cached for one hour and concurrent refreshes are coalesced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same constructor activation, scan cache, per-session call count, and concurrency limit existed before the announcement and button were renamed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The constructor starts activation asynchronously, so measurement does not block notice construction; completion controls later suggestion visibility.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Measurement scales with worktree-owning sessions only on cold scans; each visibility transition produces one fixed-size announcement. The renamed text does not change either multiplicity.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Notice updates are synchronous observable reactions. Service scans are single-flight through _refreshPromise, measurements are limited to two concurrently, and session-change refreshes are delayed by a 10-second RunOnceScheduler.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold scans measure worktrees; warm scans within one hour return without rescanning, and concurrent callers share the refresh promise. No cache behavior changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the notice constructor, autorun, and cleanup-service call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact disk-usage cost depends on the provider and number of sessions, but all expensive work is pre-existing and unaffected by this diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The replacement strings neither introduce the scan nor increase its frequency, fan-out, concurrency, or critical-path impact.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening Sessions or cleanup-editor accessibility help
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On explicit accessibility-help invocation, the providers synchronously build a fixed array of localized guidance and join it for display. The cleanup-suggestion paragraph is conditionally included after an in-process configuration read.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed paragraph count and fixed string allocation per help invocation, independent of session history and worktree count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous in-process string construction only; no asynchronous boundary, queue, or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No changed cache or coalescing behavior. The same localization keys and provider lifecycle are retained.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from both accessibility provider implementations and the changed localized literals.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; wording length changes are bounded and do not create a scaling mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff preserves invocation frequency and allocation cardinality and adds no boundary work.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all eight changed files and traced startup registration, command/editor opening, cleanup-notice activation, and accessibility-help rendering. Every production change is a localized wording replacement; existing worktree disk measurements remain cached, coalesced, and concurrency-limited exactly as before. No actionable performance regression or regression fix was found.
